children: The European Commission approved Roche’s Susvimo (ranibizumab 100 mg/mL) for treating neovascular age-related macular degeneration, enabling continuous delivery via the Contivue Port Delivery Platform.
Material Details
Detail
AI Analyst View
EC approves Susvimo for nAMD
Regulatory clearance opens the EU market for a refillable implant alternative to frequent injections.
Continuous delivery via Contivue
Differentiated delivery may drive uptake among patients seeking fewer clinic visits.
Archway showed non-inferior vision
Clinical parity to monthly IVT ranibizumab supports physician adoption.
As few as two refills per year
Lower treatment burden can expand adherence and real-world use.
Platform may add more molecules
Pipeline use on the platform could broaden indications and revenue over time.
Context by AI Analyst

This is a late-stage regulatory win extending Susvimo access beyond the US and select markets. Commercial traction, reimbursement wins across EU countries, and safety/real-world data will determine the revenue impact.

By continuously delivering medicine into the eye through the Contivue refillable implant, Susvimo is the first and only continuous delivery treatment that offers an alternative to standard-of-care eye injections for nAMD1-3
Susvimo helps people with nAMD maintain their vision with as few as two treatments per year1-3
Data from the Phase III Archway study showed that Susvimo maintained vision equivalent to monthly intravitreal ranibizumab injections2
nAMD is a leading cause of vision loss in adults over 60 and affects approximately 1.7 million people across the European Union4,5

title: Roche (RHO) Wins EU Approval for Susvimo in nAMD
